observations.text: Preview banner confirms history/analytics not saved.
Prediction six-second delay: about 200 m / about 2 km / about 20 km; chose 200 m and locked.
Before commitment, diagram text states “Each arc: one second ... 343 m (air at 20 °C).”
At zero: “Flash and thunder together: the strike is right here”; set 6: “2.06 km”, flash 0.0000069 s and “Count ÷ 3 = 2”. Screenshot showed six arcs and strike near 2 km.
Reveal preserves 12-second state, resolves original six-second answer as about 2 km, explains light versus sound, 343m/s and count divided by three.

prediction.reason: Question is answerable, but visible 343m-per-second statement cues the calculation.

interaction.reason: Zero, six and twelve seconds expose linear relation and zero boundary without changing other inputs.

payoff.reason: Reveal connects current count, arcs, speed and original answer but does not explain approximation limits beyond initial temperature label.

clarity.reason: Named slider, live distance and current-state reveal make action and result explicit.

transfer.reason: Count divided by three is an actionable rule with a concrete second delay.

accessibility.reason: No sufficient multi-mode accessibility checks; D slider Home key is only a partial keyboard observation.
evidence: Observed DOM accessible names, desktop screenshots; no comprehensive check.

surprise.reason: Committed 200m becomes 2.06km but pre-question speed cue weakens expectation reversal.

visualExplanation.reason: Arcs, strike position and axis convey zero and doubled-distance states.

playfulness.reason: Continuous reversible delay control supports experimentation.

practicalValue.reason: Rule estimates distance from an everyday observable delay.

depth.reason: Sound propagation, negligible light travel and proportional distance are linked.

complexity.reason: Read seconds/km and relate doubled count to doubled distance; no prior propagation theory needed.
complexity.boundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain theory assumed.

whyCool: Doubling the delay from six to twelve seconds moves the strike from 2.06 to 4.12 km.
caveat: No actual flash/thunder timing or audio tested; temperature dependence not explored.
